text: In summer (literally: "the hot time"), an ant (literally: "a little black animal") was always working. It looked for food and carried it home. A grasshopper (literally: "a big green animal") didn't work. It played, chatted, and laughed. The grasshopper said: "Why are you working? Come and play!" The ant said: "Winter will come. I need to have food." The grasshopper laughed: "Winter is far away!" Then winter came. The ground was all white. The grasshopper was cold, had nothing to eat, and was very unhappy. It went to the ant's house and asked: "Can you give me a little food?" The ant said: "What were you doing in the summer?" The grasshopper said: "I was playing." The ant gave it a little food and said: "Next summer, you work too!"

blind.whole: A small black animal works all through the hot season, gathering food and taking it home. A big green animal does not work. It plays, chats and laughs, and asks the small one why it bothers working. The small animal says the cold season will come and it needs food. The big one laughs that the cold season is far away. Then the cold season comes, the ground turns white, and the big animal is cold, has no food and is unhappy. It goes to the small animal's home and asks for a little food. The small animal asks what it was doing in the hot season, and it says it was playing. The small animal gives it a little food and says that next hot season it must work too. The point is to work and get ready for hard times ahead.
blind.unsure: Sentence 22: 'Tā shuō' does not say who speaks. I read it as the small animal, since it just gave the food and the words are a lesson to the big one. It could also be the big animal promising 'next hot time, you (meaning I) will work too', but that fits the 'nǐ' less well. Sentence 11: 'yào' could be 'want' or 'need'. Both fit. The two animals are never named, only described as 'small and black' and 'big and plant-coloured'. The story suggests particular creatures, but nothing in the text says which. Sentence 2: I read 'shénme shí-jiān dōu' as 'at any time, all the time'. Some glosses gave the wrong sense, though the right one was clear from context: 'shí-jiān' came out as 'ten-between' (it means time), 'yī-diǎn' as 'one o'clock' (it means a little), 'zhǎo' as 'to hunt' (here it means look for), 'tā' as 'he' (here it means it), 'dì-shàng' as 'floor-up' (here it means on the ground), and 'méi-yǒu' as a long particle note (it means does not have).

notes: Translated by hand following the translate skill, at the level of the whole dictionary (2026-10-22). kb_memory gave the book's own lines of this story (most at 57-100% shared), so most sentences adapt them; the changes: green is the dictionary's zhíwù-de yánsè (the book's lines say tiān-de yánsè, the colour of the sky, which reads as blue); work is gōng-zuò (work-do) where the book has zuò, which alone reads as do; each quote that held two sentences, and each long line, is split; chī-de dōng-xi became chī-de and nǐ wèi-shénme zài gōng-zuò lost its zài, since both gave over 500 readings; the animals are named zhè-ge xiǎo dòng-wù and zhè-ge dà dòng-wù after their first description (the book: hēi-sè-de dòng-wù, tiān-de yánsè-de dòng-wù). Tried and dropped: "Rè-de shí-jiān, yǒu yī-ge hēi-sè-de xiǎo dòng-wù." reads only as a call (Time , S needs a sentence with a doer, and one that starts with yǒu has none), so the ant comes first in a sentence of its own; "Rè-de shí-jiān, tā shénme shí-jiān dōu zài gōng-zuò." and "Rè-de shí-jiān, yī-ge hēi-sè-de xiǎo dòng-wù zài gōng-zuò." have no time reading among the first 500 (without zài the first has one, reading 109); "Hòu-lái, lěng-de shí-jiān lái le." reads hòu-lái only as a call or as hòu + lái (no Time rule has it), so jiù says then; "Hái yǒu yī-ge zhíwù-de yánsè-de dà dòng-wù." is 11 words at depth 2, so the colour got its own sentence; "Nǐ néng gěi wǒ yī-diǎn ma?" never reads yī-diǎn as a bit (the Bit rule needs a verb or describing word before it), while yī-diǎn chī-de reads as a number, counting word and thing (gěi wǒ [yī diǎn chī-de]). For the author: kb_gloss glosses diǎn as o'clock, so yī-diǎn chī-de shows as "one o'clock to eat" to the blind reader; kb_lookup has nothing for unhappy (bù kāi-xīn, from the book, says it); kb_lookup grasshopper lists alcohol (ràng-tóu-biàn-luàn-de shuǐ) as a kind-of. Not said, by choice: le in gave (the narration stays in plain verbs, as the book's own story lines do for most verbs). Glossary proposal: summer -> rè-de shí-jiān: the pair of winter's own form lěng-de shí-jiān, 4 words against the 7 of nián-lǐ zuì rè-de shí-jiān. Glossary proposal: next summer -> xià-yī-ge rè-de shí-jiān: next-last-time reads xià-yī-ge before a time as one time phrase (its own example), then a comma. Glossary proposal: then (the next thing in a story) -> jiù before the verb: Hòu-lái at the front reads only as a call. Glossary proposal: unhappy -> bù kāi-xīn: kb_lookup finds nothing for unhappy; the book says not happy. Translated before kb_memory hid the stories' own lines (HAOSHUODE_MEMORY_SKIP), so some sentences reuse the book's lines and the book overlap is higher than a fresh run would give.
